subject: the MILL
statement: No mill dimension exists anywhere in the mined corpus - not in Viollet's Dictionnaire (cycle 42 sweep) and not in Addy. Slot 11 is held open to force the sourcing decision; any mill asset built now would have NO dimensional authority.

subject: breadth != roof span for aisled/cruck buildings
statement: The Bolsterstone section (inspected at full resolution) is a cruck truss with outshuts: the main roof spans between the blades, not the walls, and no single pitch describes the section. Any pitch derived from breadth/2 on an aisled building is UNSAFE.
where_recorded: addy1898 n109 (printed 75), VERIFIED; roof_pitch_derived safety flags

subject: the long yoke
statement: The Welsh Laws give the long yoke as 16 ft (i.187, i.539), 16 1/2 ft (ii.784) and 15 1/2 ft (ii.852). Addy prints all without resolving; all rows carried under conflict_group=long-yoke.

subject: Gwilt's stair pitch
statement: The same printed page (668) carries a constant tread x riser product of 66 AND Newland's pairing table, which violates it by up to 47% at the extremes. Both carried under conflict_group=gwilt-stair-pitch.

subject: Cholsey barn '51 feet high'
statement: Addy (quoting Parker) prints 303 ft long and 51 ft HIGH; the usual published figure for Cholsey is a WIDTH of about 54 ft. Probably a slip for 'wide' - recorded as printed, never silently corrected.

subject: Coucy donjon height
statement: 64 m (from the ditch bottom, stated), 65 m (same article's footnote, 'environ'), 55 m (the Donjon article, datum unchecked - open queue item). Rows carried verbatim; no canonical height may be chosen until the datums are resolved.

subject: Carcassonne / Pierrefonds dimensions
statement: Both are Viollet's own restoration sites: any crenel sill, hoarding or embrasure measured there is his WORK, not medieval fabric. Rows flagged uncertainty_type=provenance; the older-manifest re-class remains an open queue item.
where_recorded: building_bom BC-07B rows; findings queue item 3

subject: the Kensworth conjectural plan
statement: Addy's 'drawn to scale' plan measures only approximately to scale (lengths ~4%, breadths ~8%, axes differing ~12%); it yields NO number the text does not already state. Topology reference only.
